QuestionGroups.PassageHtml:
Remote Work Transforms Corporate Culture

Business Weekly | July 2026

The shift to remote work has fundamentally changed how companies operate around the world. A recent survey of 2,000 companies found that 68% now offer some form of flexible working arrangement, up from just 23% in 2019.

Many organizations report increased productivity among remote workers. However, challenges remain, particularly in maintaining team cohesion and company culture. Some firms have responded by introducing "hybrid" models, which combine in-office and remote working days.

"The key is finding the right balance," says Dr. Linda Park, a workplace psychology expert. "Employees who have flexibility tend to show higher job satisfaction and lower turnover rates."

Despite the benefits, some executives remain unconvinced. A quarter of companies surveyed still require full-time office attendance, citing concerns about collaboration and oversight.

Questions.Text: What percentage of companies offered flexible working in 2019?
According to Dr. Linda Park, what do flexible employees experience?
What is the main concern of companies that still require full office attendance?

QuestionGroups.PassageHtml:
Companies Embrace Sustainable Practices

An increasing number of corporations are integrating sustainability into their core business strategies. According to a 2026 Global Business Report, over 75% of Fortune 500 companies now have dedicated sustainability teams, compared to 45% a decade ago.

Driving this shift is a combination of consumer demand, regulatory pressure, and growing evidence that sustainable practices can improve long-term profitability. Green investments often lead to reduced operating costs through energy efficiency, waste reduction, and supply chain optimization.

"Sustainability is no longer optional," said Maria González, CEO of EcoVentures. "It is a business imperative that attracts top talent, strengthens brand loyalty, and opens new market opportunities."

Critics, however, point out that many companies engage in "greenwashing" — making misleading claims about their environmental practices. Regulators in the EU and US have begun cracking down, imposing fines on companies that overstate their sustainability credentials.

Despite these challenges, experts agree that the trend toward sustainability will continue to grow, reshaping the competitive landscape across industries for years to come.

Questions.Text: What percentage of Fortune 500 companies had sustainability teams a decade ago?
According to the article, what does sustainability attract?

QuestionGroups.PassageHtml:
The Rise of the Four-Day Workweek

Companies in Iceland, Japan, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom have piloted four-day workweek programs, and the results have been largely positive. Employees report higher job satisfaction, reduced burnout, and improved work-life balance. Employers, meanwhile, have observed maintained or increased productivity levels.

Microsoft Japan's pilot program showed a 40% increase in productivity when employees worked four days a week. The company attributed this to fewer unnecessary meetings and more focused work hours.

Not all industries are suited to a four-day model, however. Sectors such as healthcare, emergency services, and retail often require continuous coverage. Experts suggest that flexible arrangements, rather than a rigid four-day week, may be the solution for such industries.

As debate continues, one thing is clear: the traditional 9-to-5, five-day workweek is being reconsidered in boardrooms around the world.

Questions.Text: What did Microsoft Japan's pilot program show?
Which sector is NOT mentioned as unsuitable for a four-day week?

Global Trade Fair Returns to Geneva

The Geneva International Trade Fair (GITF) is set to return this October after a two-year hiatus. Organizers expect over 10,000 participants from 80 countries, making it one of the largest trade events of the decade.

The fair will feature exhibitions from sectors including technology, manufacturing, renewable energy, and consumer goods. A series of keynote speeches by industry leaders will be held alongside the exhibitions, covering topics such as AI integration in business and global supply chain resilience.

Companies wishing to exhibit must apply by August 31. Booth sizes range from 10 to 100 square meters, with pricing starting at $500 per square meter. Early applicants will receive a 20% discount on booth costs.

Visitors can register online starting September 1 at www.gitf2026.org. General admission is free, while VIP passes offering access to exclusive networking events cost $250.
